Supersedes the auth and onboarding halves of docs 14, 15 and 21. Current as of 3 Aug 2026.

Drawn in the Omelette project `Macros Tracker Native setup` as `AuthFlow.dc.html` and `Onboarding.dc.html`, on the turn-9 board in `Macros Tracker App.dc.html`. Exports in `exports/for-linear-turn9/`.

Two changes, and the second is the one that matters. Apple-only auth removes three screens. Resequencing onboarding behind the first meal removes the worst activation shape in the product — demanding effort before demonstrating value.

## The sequence

```
9a Welcome
  → 9b Apple sheet
  → 9c Verifying
  → 9g first capture        (doc 27)
  → 9j first review         (doc 27)
  → 9d "set targets so we can track this"
  → 9e six questions
  → 9f your targets
  → Today
```

Auth is three screens where it was four, and only one of them is ours. Onboarding sits *after* the first logged meal.

---

## What changed, and why the screens changed with it

### Auth is one action

Register and login are the same call, so the Register / Log in toggle on `6b` was answering a question the user is no longer asked. Welcome is now a wordmark, a sentence and one button.

The copy under the button does the work the toggle used to: *signing in and signing up are the same action*. Without it, a returning user hesitates over whether they are about to make a second account.

### The Apple sheet is drawn even though it is not ours

Two reasons. It is a screen the user unambiguously sees, so leaving it out makes the sequence read shorter than it is. And the **Hide My Email** row is the visual argument for the `apple_user_id` join key — the one detail on this path that is expensive to get wrong.

The annotation on `9b` names the first-authorization trap directly: name and email arrive **only** on that first authorization. It is a bug that is invisible until the second user signs in, and impossible to fix retroactively.

### Verifying is a real screen, not a spinner

A second or two of JWKS fetch, signature validation and claim checks, drawn as three named lines rather than an indeterminate spinner — same principle as the analyze state in doc 06. A frozen view during a slow call reads as a crash.

It also replaces the entire verify-email stack, and with it the trap doc 04 describes: a blocking email inside an unexitable onboarding stack, where an undelivered message left a user with no path forward.

### The bridge screen is new, and the resequencing needs it

`9d` did not exist in any prior doc. Moving the questions after the first meal creates a moment that has to be designed: the user has just watched a photo turn into three numbers, and now has to be asked for six answers.

The screen shows **their own first entry at the top** — not a generic illustration. The ask is legible because the payoff is directly above it.

**Not now is a real exit.** Doc 05 says onboarding can be skipped or abandoned and the app still works. That is only true if the screen says so, so the copy states the consequence: macros still log, nothing scores until targets exist.

### Six questions, not ten

Goal weight, timeline, training days and dietary constraints are gone — none are inputs to Mifflin-St Jeor. The screen is otherwise unchanged from `6e`, minus the free-text control, which existed only for the dietary-constraints question. The `isText` branch has been removed from the component rather than left dormant.

---

## Decisions

**The stack is exitable now.** Doc 21 described flow 01 as a modal that cannot be exited, which was correct when a half-onboarded account had no coherent state. It does now: a user with entries and no targets is a sensible thing to be. Back from question one returns to `9d` rather than to nowhere.

**Welcome carries no legal wall.** One line about photos going to an AI provider, in the dimmest text on the screen. It is true, it is the only surprising thing about the data flow, and it belongs before the tap rather than in a settings page.

**No returning-user variant of Welcome.** The button is identical either way; the server decides. Drawing two states that differ in nothing would imply a branch the code does not have.

---

## Gaps and open questions

**Where does the first capture come from on a cold start?** `9c` ends on `LOG YOUR FIRST MEAL`, which pushes straight into capture. Right shape, but it means a brand-new user meets the camera permission prompt within about four seconds of installing. Worth deciding whether that prompt deserves a sentence of context first, given doc 06's rule that camera is the permission that must succeed.

**Backfilling null** `target_version` **is invisible.** Doc 05 specifies it; no screen mentions it. Probably correct — but if someone logs a week before setting targets, those days silently acquire retroactive scoring, which may surprise them in History.

**Skipping targets has no second prompt.** Take *Not now* and there is no path back to `9d` except Settings. For a user who skipped on day one and now wants a ring, Settings › Targets is discoverable but not offered. A dismissible row on Today would cost little.
